fullDescription: A loud two-colour event deck built around a single band rotated off-axis that runs out of both side edges and carries the headline inside it. The band is the layout, not a decoration: it turns 90 degrees into a panel divider on the content slide, and the closer inverts ground and ink. Heavy geometric monospace display type, hand-drawn squiggles and one hard-shadowed sticker badge do the rest. Good for zine fairs, markets, club nights, workshops, student shows and any programme that should feel printed rather than filed.
prompt:
## Resumo
A two-colour event deck whose entire layout is one colour band rotated off-axis, running out of both side edges with the headline set inside it.

## Estilo Visual
Apply a bold two-colour poster style. Palette: ground #FFD84D, ink #221C4A, plus the ink at 60/30% for secondary copy. Exactly two colours; the closer swaps which is ground and which is ink. Typography: 'Rubik Mono One' for every display line at line-height 0.94 and letter-spacing -0.02em; 'Space Grotesk' 500-700 for body and for corner metadata, uppercase at letter-spacing 0.22em. AVOID a yellow-green or chartreuse — an acid yellow-green against a blue-violet is the single most generated-looking bold palette there is; keep the yellow WARM. DO NOT add a gradient, a glow, or a third accent colour.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Cover
A band in the ink colour, wider than the stage (left:-160px, width 2240px) and about 450px tall, rotated -6.5 degrees so it exits both side edges. Set the title as two centred lines in the mono display face at about 158px, in the ground colour, sitting inside the band. Above the band, flush LEFT, a tracked-caps line and a hand-drawn squiggle. Below it, a centred date line in the display face at 64px and a rotated sticker badge straddling the band's lower edge. Corner metadata bottom-left and bottom-right. Watch the band's rotation: it rises roughly 110px by the right edge, so a full-width centred line placed near it will be swallowed — keep upper copy left-aligned and high.

### Programme
Stand the same band up as a tall rotated slab occupying the right third, still at -6.5 degrees. Left field: a two-line display heading at 104px, a short lede in the 60% ink, and a schedule list of four rows on a two-column grid — a mono time at 30px against a 29px title with a small uppercase room label beneath, each row closed by a heavy 3px rule. Right, inside the slab: one enormous figure at about 172px in the ground colour with a short caption under it. A rotated sticker straddles the slab's edge near the bottom. Keep the sticker's hard offset shadow fully inside the canvas.

### Closer
Swap the colours: ink ground, sunflower type, no band. Two centred display lines at about 196px, a two-line venue and date block at 28px below, and one centred sticker badge. Corner metadata as before. Keep it plain — the whole point is that the band's absence reads as an ending.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### The rotated band — The layout itself, not an ornament laid on top of one.
One flat rectangle in the ink colour, deliberately wider and taller than it needs to be so that after rotate(-6.5deg) it still runs off both side edges with no corner gap. Content sits INSIDE it, not merely near it: the headline on the cover, the figure on the programme slide. Reuse the same angle on every slide it appears on — one consistent angle reads as a decision, two angles read as an accident.

### Sticker badge — A rotated pill with a hard offset shadow, straddling the band's edge.
A pill in the ground colour with a 3px ink border, a 999px radius, 16px by 34px padding and a HARD offset shadow (8px 8px 0, no blur) in the ink. Rotate it a few degrees and place it so it crosses the band's edge, half on each colour. On the inverted closer drop the shadow entirely rather than tinting it — a same-hue translucent shadow on a dark ground just reads as dirt. Keep the shadow inside the canvas: a rotated badge clipped by the frame edge is the classic failure here.

### Hand-drawn squiggle — The one organic mark against all the geometry.
An inline SVG path — a single wavy stroke, 9px wide with round caps, in the ink colour. Use it two or three times per deck at most, mirrored with scaleX(-1) for variety, in otherwise empty corners. It is punctuation, not texture; do not tile it and do not build a pattern from it.
